record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: Let the test Volterra functional integro-differential equation (4.8) have asymptotically stable exact solutions. If it is solved on a uniform mesh by collocation in S^{(0)}_m(I_h), for which collocation parameters {c_i} does the collocation solution u_h(t) also satisfy \lim_{t	o\infty} u_h(t)=0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.2 (b) Let (4.8) be such that its solutions u are asymptotically stable. If this test VFIDE is solved by collocation in S(0) m (Ih), with uniform mesh Ih, for which collocation parameters {ci} does lim t	o\infty uh(t)=0 hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the linear test Volterra functional integro-differential equation with proportional (vanishing) delay
  u'(t) = a u(t) + b u(qt) + ∫_0^t K_1(t,s) u(s) ds + ∫_0^{qt} K_2(t,s) u(s) ds,  t ≥ 0,
  u(0) = u_0,
where a, b ∈ ℝ, 0 < q < 1, and K_1, K_2 are continuous kernels, chosen so that every exact solution u is asymptotically stable, i.e. lim_{t→∞} u(t) = 0.

Fix m ≥ 1 and m distinct collocation parameters 0 < c_1 < c_2 < … < c_m ≤ 1. On the uniform mesh I_h = {t_n = nh : n = 0,1,2,…} with stepsize h > 0, define the piecewise-polynomial space
  S_m^{(0)}(I_h) = { v ∈ C([0,∞)) : v|_{[t_n, t_{n+1}]} is a polynomial of degree ≤ m for all n ≥ 0 }.
Let u_h ∈ S_m^{(0)}(I_h) denote the collocation solution determined by imposing the equation at the collocation points t_{n,i} := t_n + c_i h (i = 1,…,m; n = 0,1,2,…), where the delayed term u_h(q t_{n,i}) and the memory integrals are evaluated by exact (or analytically defined) interpolation/integration of u_h.

Problem. Characterize the set of collocation parameters {c_1,…,c_m} ⊂ (0,1] for which, for every stepsize h > 0 and every initial value u_0, the collocation solution satisfies
  lim_{t→∞} u_h(t) = 0.
artifact.category_tag: Collocation methods for delay Volterra equations
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in surveys on the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays. Subsequent work (e.g., on asymptotic stability of collocation methods for pantograph-type DDEs and VFIDEs) has addressed special cases—showing, for instance, that A-stability of the ODE-collocation method on geometric meshes can be inherited—but a complete characterization of the parameters {c_i} ensuring discrete asymptotic stability on uniform meshes for the VFIDE test equation does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems include stability of collocation solutions on uniform meshes for VFIDEs with proportional delay qt.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic stability question for collocation in S_m^{(0)}(I_h) on uniform meshes is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Stability of collocation methods for delay differential equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: A-stability of ODE collocation implies asymptotic stability for pantograph DDE collocation.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for the pure-delay (no Volterra memory) case but not the full VFIDE.

status_evidence.title: On the asymptotic stability of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Continuous-level stability conditions for VFIDEs with vanishing delays.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous-time stability is addressed, but a complete discrete characterization for collocation on uniform meshes remains unresolved.
